NEPOCORE / PRACTICAL LEARNING GUIDES

Turn your own spelling list into useful practice

By Nabin Kunwar · Published November 4, 2026 · Product usage guide

A custom spelling worksheet is useful when its words connect to the learner's actual reading or classwork. Start with a short list you have permission to use. Enter words separated by commas; the tool keeps up to sixteen distinct entries.

Choose a manageable list

Six familiar words and two new ones can be a practical starting point. For example, garden, flower, cloud, rain, sunshine and spring connect to a shared topic. The right list depends on current lessons rather than a fixed age label.

Say, look, cover, write, check

Read a word aloud and discuss what it means. Look closely at its letter sequence. Cover the printed model with paper, write the word on the answer line, then uncover the model and compare. The generator prints the word as a model; it does not hide it automatically or run a digital dictation test.

Notice a pattern

For rain and train, underline the shared letter pattern. Then discuss meaning in a sentence. A spelling list alone cannot show whether a learner understands a word, so include a brief spoken example or reading activity.

Use a word search as an extra activity

The same list can become a word search when every entry contains two to twelve English letters. Spaces and punctuation are removed in word-search mode. Preview the final word list before printing. Finding a word is a recognition activity; it should not be the only check of independent spelling.

Respect language differences

Enter colour or color according to the variety of English being taught. Region does not translate or correct spelling. For accented letters or another script, use the spelling sheet and browser Print / Save as PDF rather than the English-only word search.
